text:
maya: FYI hit a production GPU shortage in eu-west-1 — autoscaler didn't cycle new GPU nodepool.
liam: ugh, details? capacity or scheduling failure?
sophia: saw pods Pending with message: "no nodes are available that match taints/tolerations" earlier today.
maya: root cause looks like our terraform module changed the node-label key during the refactor. cluster-autoscaler is filtering by label. new nodepool created with label `redwood.com/gpu-type=rtx6000` but ca expects `redwood.com/gpu=rtx`.
arin: timeline: created nodepool at 08:12, first Pending at 08:18, scale-up triggered but CA ignored because label mismatch.
liam: any dry-run of the autoscaler config? can we see logs from the ca pod?
maya: pasted CA logs snippet:
```
I0308 08:19:02.123456       1 scale_up.go:130] NodeGroup "ng-gpu-eu-1" is not autoscalable: node labels mismatch: expecting key=redwood.com/gpu
I0308 08:19:02.123789       1 scale_up.go:145] No options for scaling up
```
sophia: oof. terraform change #4567 swapped label map to be more descriptive, missed CA mapping in helm values.
liam: immediate remediation: patch the existing nodepool label to the expected key so CA can see it. We can `kubectl label nodes --all`? wait need to target the instances.
arin: better to change the node resource's label via cloud provider so it survives node restart (kubelet labels are ephemeral). For AKS/GKE you'd use instance templates. For our current infra (eks), label on nodegroup launch config or use `aws eks update-nodegroup-config`.
maya: hotfix plan I applied: rolled nodepool via terraform taint on one instance, replaced instance with corrected label using aws cli and then CA picked it up and scaled for ~10 minutes. But we still have drift in terraform state.
liam: we need a root fix in code. Proposal:
- update terraform module to emit label `redwood.com/gpu` (legacy key) in addition to new descriptive key
- update cluster-autoscaler helm values to accept both labels (or remove label-based filter and use nodegroup name)
- add unit test to tf module to validate label keys
- add a post-deploy helm test that checks CA sees all nodegroups
sophia: agree. Also add helm value `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false`? not related here though.
arin: CA supports `--node-group-auto-discovery` with tags; we could switch CA discovery to tag-based instead of label-based. For AWS use tag: `k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled` and `k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/<ASGName>`.
liam: switching to tag discovery is safer long-term. Less brittle to label drift. But bigger change across clouds. We should do quick dual-support: labels + tags.
maya: terraform hotfix diff I will open. Minimal patch to the module:
```
resource "aws_launch_template" "gpu" {
  tag_specifications = [{ key = "k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled", value = "true" }, { key = "redwood.com/gpu", value = var.gpu_type }]
  additional_tag = { "redwood.com/gpu-type" = var.gpu_type }
}
```
liam: also update helm values for CA in our chart:
```
autoscaler:
  extraArgs:
    --nodes-labels=redwood.com/gpu,redwood.com/gpu-type
```
sophia: make sure to run `helm upgrade --install` in staging; add an integration test where we create a fake nodepool and assert CA recognizes it.
arin: ops checklist for rollout:
- patch tf module in a feature branch
- apply in staging, create gpu nodepool with new label and verify CA scales
- plan/apply in prod with a small batch and monitor console
- if drift found, run script to add legacy label to existing nodepools
maya: monitoring: added dashboard tile for CA ignored-nodegroups by parsing CA logs + a CloudWatch metric on `IgnoredNodeGroups` (custom metric). alerted on >0 for 5m.
liam: cost note: some nodepools ended up underutilized during the incident, we charged extra for 3 hours. please put a flag in the terraform module to enable `max_unneeded_percentage` for CA (reduce overprovisioning).
sophia: also add docs in ops runbook: How to reconcile label drift, commands for aws cli to patch launch template or ASG tags, and rollback steps.
deploy-bot: Deployment: branch "fix/ca-label-dual-support" created by maya, CI passed, ready for review.
maya: will open PR with the tf + helm updates + test. tagging @liam @sophia for review. thanks all :thumbsup:
